patterns.action: Keep one rule: the player sees a gap or hazard, commits to a move, lands or fails, and is back at the last checkpoint within seconds.
patterns.statement: The game is the move, commit, land cycle repeated

patterns.condition: Respawn after a fall or a trap
patterns.action: Store each player's last checkpoint in a map keyed by player and respawn from it, updating it only when a later checkpoint is touched in order.
patterns.statement: Checkpoints must be remembered for each player

patterns.action: Respawn within about two seconds at the checkpoint without losing items, so the cost of failing is the time lost and never a long wait.

patterns.condition: A new obstacle type first appears
patterns.action: Show each new mechanic in a safe spot with no kill below it, then use it alone, then combine it with older ones.
patterns.statement: Difficulty walls come from mechanics that were never taught

patterns.condition: Traps in a deathrun with a trapper role
patterns.action: Warn with a short sound or visual before a trap hits, keep trap cycles readable, and limit how often the trapper can fire.
Measure the longest gap a normal jump clears by testing, then build the hardest gap at roughly 85 percent of it so a clean attempt always works.
patterns.statement: A jump tuned to the very edge looks broken

patterns.condition: Open geometry that could be bypassed
patterns.action: Close shortcuts with barriers or kill volumes, or keep them on purpose and reward them, and require checkpoints in order so a skipped section is noticed.

patterns.condition: A time trial or speedrun course
patterns.action: Show a run time for each player, store the best time per player, and show it at the end so players can beat themselves.
patterns.statement: A visible run time drives replay

patterns.condition: Using many moving or animated obstacles
patterns.action: Use movers where they change the decision, not as decoration, and keep many movers to a single section at a time.
patterns.statement: Moving platforms cost more than static ones

patterns.condition: Planning how long the map lasts
patterns.action: Plan eight to twelve short stages of about a minute each, end with a finish line and a result screen, and make replaying easy.
patterns.statement: Stage count and length set the session time

patterns.condition: Building the visual side of a course
patterns.action: Make landing surfaces contrast with hazards by color and light, and keep the next target visible from the takeoff spot.
patterns.statement: Hazards must read against the background

patterns.action: Start from each checkpoint and finish the run, check that falling in each section returns to the right place, and that nothing can trap a player.
patterns.statement: Test the whole run from every checkpoint
